representations.raw:
- D: Added two tests to `tests/test_session_schema.py` asserting seed-side consistency in both
  directions: every `- skill: <name>` in the seed trigger registry has both a file under
  `memory_seed/seed/.memory-seed/skills/` and a `SeedFile` destination in `core.SEED_FILES`; and every
  `.memory-seed/skills/*.md` destination in `SEED_FILES` (excluding `index.md`, which is the registry
  itself) is registered. Two module-level helpers extract the name lists.
- R: This closes the gap that let `developer-rendered-ui-debugging.md` ship as a registry entry with no
  installed file - a fresh `memory-seed init` wrote a trigger map pointing at a skill it never
  installed. The existing `test_universal_registry_entries_have_live_and_seed_skill_files` *looks* like
  it covers direction 1, but its `if "persona:" in body: continue` skips exactly the persona entries
  the defect lived in, and it never consults `SEED_FILES` at all. The new tests deliberately drop that
  skip and are seed-only: the skip is legitimate for the live runtime (optional/persona skills are
  installed conditionally) but wrong for the seed, which ships everything unconditionally. Left the
  live-runtime side to the existing test rather than widening it.
- A: Considered the derived-list refactor the gap really argues for - adding a skill still needs manual
  edits in five places (`SEED_FILES`, `pyproject.toml` package-data, the expected-destinations list in
  `test_memory_seed.py`, `SKILL_PROFILES`, `SKILL_DESCRIPTIONS`). Out of scope here; the test makes the
  most damaging of those five drift loud, and the refactor stays a separate call.
- F: `tests/test_session_schema.py` (only changed file; uncommitted).
- T: `python -m pytest tests -q` - 641 passed, 14 subtests passed. A green run proves nothing on its own
  here, since all three legs are currently consistent, so verified the tests actually bite by mutating
  each leg in isolation and confirming the matching assertion fires: (A) `SeedFile` entry removed ->
  fails on the `SEED_FILES` assert; (B) seed skill file deleted -> fails on the exists assert;

representations.raw:
- D: Record two candidate fixes ahead of the band in priority: raise the semantic blend weight
  (`semantic_component = cosine * 3.0`, `semantic_cache.py:927`), and re-examine the recency
  multiplier. Neither is applied in this branch - both need their own held-out fit.
- R: Semantic ranking is on by default and changes paraphrase recall by exactly zero - 63/120 in
  the top 8 with it on and off. The reason is arithmetic: cosine is bounded by 1, so a perfect
  semantic match contributes 3.0 against one tag match's 12.0, and the measured semantic share of
  `match_score` is 21.6%. It cannot reorder anything separated by more than three lexical points.

  paraphrase recall from 62% to 78% at weight 60, turning over by 120, so the optimum is a real
  interior point and the signal was there all along. Separately, chasing a 73-versus-63 discrepancy
  between two of my own harnesses isolated the recency multiplier: it removes 10 of 120 correct
  answers from the top 8. In a store whose purpose is retrieving old decisions, down-weighting age
  deserves an explicit argument, and `lambda_days=0.01` has never been validated against recall.
  Together these are worth more than any abstention label, because a perfect band on 62% recall
  correctly reports "nothing found" while the answer sits in the store.

  held-out split, so it is an order of magnitude rather than a constant, and `ranking-ab` cannot

title: D1 - Adopt four Codex harness constants, each forced by an observed failure

representations.raw:
- D: The Codex runner passes `-c projects={"<run dir>"={trust_level="trusted"}}`,
  `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, `-c features.apps=false`, and pins the MCP server's
  `cwd` to the run directory per run rather than in the template.
- R: None is cosmetic. Codex loads project-scoped `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json` only
  for trusted paths and every run directory is a fresh untrusted path, so without the trust
  override L0 has no write path and L2/L3 have no hooks. `approval_policy="never"` does not cover
  MCP tool calls - a probe with it set returned `user cancelled MCP tool call` - so the approvals
  bypass is the only headless route, the direct analogue of Claude's `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
  This machine's Codex exposes 240 MCP tools costing ~139k input tokens of tool surface per turn;
  `features.apps=false` removes them while leaving the memory-seed server intact. And the stock MCP
  entry leaves `cwd` unset, which matters because the server resolves `cwd="."` against its own
  process cwd (H4) while `resolve_runtime` walks upward with no boundary guard (H1) - unpinned, a
  write could silently land in the PARENT store while the agent reported success.
- A: The whole-table `projects={...}` form was chosen over the dotted
  `projects.<path>.trust_level` path because the dotted-path parser splits on `.` and would break on
  any path containing one. `--ignore-user-config` was tested as a way to get a clean environment
  independent of the user's config drift and rejected: it drops the project layer too, so the
  memory-seed server disappeared. `--disable apps` (the flag form) was rejected in favour of
  `-c features.apps=false` after the model's self-reported tool list proved unreliable in both
  directions - the question was only settled by making an actual `memory_topics_list` call.
  `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` was NOT adopted: the probe showed injected trust already covers
  hook trust, so carrying it would have been an assumed rather than a demonstrated constant.
- F: `experiments/agent-capture/run.py`, `experiments/agent-capture/generate_fixtures.py`.
- T: Fixture determinism re-verified for all four Codex levels (byte-identical tree hashes across a
  regeneration); parent `links check` (153 files) and `docs check` (191 files) both OK.

- D: The Trail's loaded window is pinned into the Graph. `Service.graph()` takes `pinned_ids`:
  additive, **exempt from `limit`**, and expanded depth-1 over the lifecycle edges actually being

  dot. The visible-edge cap now tracks the grown node count instead of staying at `limit`. Exposed
  as a comma-separated `pinned_ids` query param on `/api/v1/graph/projection`. Client-side, the
  Trail's windowing rule moved into `windowedTrailNodes` and is shared with the new
  `trailWindowEntryIds`, and `switchToGraphView` refetches when the pin set has grown past what the
  current payload was fetched with.
- R: JNL: entries loaded in the Trail should always be visible in the Graph, and "Load older" should
  preload the newly appearing entries with their relationship links. The two views ranked
  differently — the Trail is a recency window, the Graph a connectivity-ranked slice — so equal
  counts (`TRAIL_WINDOW_STEP` 60, graph limit 60) still disagreed about *membership*. The decisive
  defect was in `switchToGraphView`, which refetched only when `graph === null`: growing the window
  and switching back reused a payload that predated the growth, so the map silently omitted entries
  the user had just loaded. `limit` is a ranking budget — what to volunteer — never a claim about
  what the user may see, which is why pinning overrides it rather than competing with it. Expansion
  is restricted to edge types currently switched on, since pulling in a node whose only tie is
  filtered off would draw an unexplained dot.
